answer: A garden of trust grows slowly: an identity earns weight only through sustained, reciprocal exchanges with many independent peers over weeks, not at registration. Each completed service adds a small, dated record, like a sonnet added to a shared anthology, and graph checks flag clusters that only trade among themselves. A Sybil operator could still plant fakes, but each fake needs its own long history of real work with outsiders; without it, the cluster stays quarantined in its own harbor, unable to vote or claim rewards until it proves genuine, diverse connections.
